html:
The Eyaq (Eyak) are a small Alaska Native people of the Copper River delta, around today's town of Cordova on the Gulf of Alaska. Their language is a distant relative of the Athabaskan languages; together they form the core of the Na-Dene family.

They fished the great salmon runs of the Copper River and hunted along the coast. Squeezed between the Tlingit to the east and the Sugpiaq to the west, they took on much Tlingit culture through marriage and trade.

After contact with Europeans their numbers fell to a few dozen. The Eyak language lost its last native speaker, Marie Smith Jones, in 2008. Descendants are now working to revive it.
